categories.name: VB Studio core concepts
categories.description: Extensions, App UIs, workspaces, the Designer, Express vs Advanced mode, variables, events and fragments in Visual Builder Studio for Oracle Cloud Applications.

items.name: Extensions, App UIs and configurations
items.summary: An extension delivers configurations of Oracle Cloud Application pages, new App UIs (pages and flows you build), and shared resources such as service connections, CSS or JavaScript.
items.notes: VB Studio is not a hosting platform (Git, CI/CD, issues, wiki); extensions deploy into the Fusion instance, are not iFramed, appear in Fusion menus and use the same users and roles. Visual Builder (VB/VBCS) instead hosts standalone visual applications with their own security (see https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/visual-builder-visual-builder-studio-whats-difference.html). The Unified Application is always a dependency; to reuse or configure another extension's App UIs, add that extension (not the App UI) as a dependency (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/what-are-dependencies.html). After deployment you manage the extension as a whole on the Manage Extension Lifecycle page.

items.name: Workspaces, Git repository and branches
items.summary: A workspace is your private working area: a local clone of the project's Git repo on a branch, an optional sandbox, and the target Oracle Cloud Applications environment.
items.path: Settings and Actions > Edit Page in Visual Builder Studio
items.notes: Open from a Fusion page via user menu > Settings and Actions > Edit Page in Visual Builder Studio, then pick a project (Recommended badge) and workspace. The development environment must exist in the project before a workspace can be created. Use the Git menu to commit/push, or Publish to commit, push and merge in one step; teams review through merge requests and can restrict merges to main (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/whats-extension-lifecycle.html). Sandbox = data-model changes not yet published.

items.name: Designer and Page Designer
items.summary: The Designer is VB Studio's built-in editor; the Page Designer has Live, Design and Code views plus the Components palette, Data palette, Structure view and Properties pane.
items.notes: Live shows the page as published; Design is the canvas; Code edits the page source. Test fully in Preview (new browser tab) rather than Live view. Menu > Share generates a preview URL (give testers the sandbox name too). If preview fails because VB Studio and Fusion are on different domains, Chrome's Block third-party cookies setting may need to be disabled (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/create-app-ui-or-fragment.html).

items.name: Express mode vs Advanced mode
items.summary: Express mode is a curated designer for functional administrators to tailor Oracle Cloud Applications pages; Advanced mode exposes all VB Studio features for developers. Toggle with a button in the header.
items.notes: HCM-specific: the HCM/SCM guide states 'Express mode is the only mode supported by HCM, SCM, and Procurement' and that Advanced Mode 'isn't supported by HCM, SCM, and Procurement'; if Express mode isn't available for a page, that page isn't ready to be extended in the release (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/fauvb/express-mode-in-vb-studio.html, https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/fauvb/overview-of-redwood-application-extensions.html). This statement concerns extending delivered HCM Redwood pages; confirm Oracle guidance before planning custom HCM App UIs in Advanced mode.

items.name: Variables, types and constants
items.summary: Variables hold business state bound to components by expressions; constants hold values that don't change; every variable has a built-in or custom type.
items.notes: Scopes: App UI, flow, page, fragment, layout, action chain (a fragment cannot read the outer page's variables). Types: primitives (String, Number, Boolean, Any), Object/Array, built-in, and custom types (can be created from an endpoint). Mark a page variable as Input Parameter (optionally required) to pass data on navigation or in the URL. $parameters is only for the beforeEnter event, because page variables exist from vbEnter. In code use $variables.x for the current scope, else $page.variables.x / $application.variables.x.

examples.title: Two-way and one-way binding

items.name: Events and event listeners
items.summary: Event listeners start action chains in response to lifecycle events (for example vbEnter), component events, and custom page, flow or App UI events.
items.notes: Event Listeners tab > + Event Listener > choose the event > choose or create the action chain > Finish. Choosing vbEnter creates vbEnterListener. A listener can trigger several chains (add one at a time with Add Action Chain); deleting a chain from the listener does not delete the chain. Right-click a custom event > Create Event Listener creates (eventId)Listener in the same scope.

examples.title: Component event bound to a listener
examples.code: <oj-button on-oj-action="[[ $listeners.saveClicked ]]">Save</oj-button>

items.name: Fragments
items.summary: A fragment is a reusable piece of UI that can be placed on pages, reused across App UIs in the same extension, or used as a page template.
items.notes: To use a fragment from another extension, add that extension as a dependency. Defer rendering (for example an edit panel) to speed up initial page load. At runtime $fragment.info.id is the id set on the oj-vb-fragment component (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-page-model/built-variables.html). The Unified Application fragments ask-oracle-bo-metadata and ask-oracle-chat are internal and cannot be customized or referenced.

categories.name: Rule sets, dynamic UI and business rules
categories.description: Display logic for dynamic tables, forms and containers, VB Studio business rules for validation, and the HCM Express-mode business rules and page properties.

items.name: Dynamic components, rule sets and layouts
items.summary: Dynamic tables, forms and containers render fields chosen at runtime by a rule set: display-logic rules pick a layout based on user role, device or data.
items.notes: Documented example: rule isSalesManager checks role ORA_ZBS_SALES_MANAGER_JOB and shows managerLayout; otherwise the next rule (isAuthenticatedAndTablet) is evaluated, ending with the default rule at the bottom (rules read top-down). Dynamic tables/forms can appear on many pages; a dynamic container is scoped to one page (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-applications/what-are-dynamic-components.html). Open from Properties pane > Suggested Actions > Open Rule Set Editor. HCM caution: 'Extensibility is disabled for any dynamic components used in HCM Redwood pages' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/fauvb/overview-of-redwood-application-extensions.html).

items.name: Business Rules: Validate Field Values
items.summary: Declarative validation rules on a form: define conditions, a message (Summary/Details), a severity and target fields.
items.notes: Steps: Properties pane > Business Rules > Validate Field Values > new Regular rule > Edit conditions > + Message > Severity > Target Fields. Error blocks submission; Warning only informs. With no target field and several fields, or with several target fields, the message isn't shown inline. Works only in forms rendered with oj-dyn-form, not the older oj-dynamic-form. In field templates, messages are exposed through $messages.

items.name: HCM Redwood: Business Rules and Page Properties (Express mode)
items.summary: For HCM Redwood pages, Express mode offers Business Rules (Configure Fields and Regions; Validate Field Values) and Page Properties (constants) to tailor delivered pages.
items.path: Redwood page > Settings and Actions > Edit Page in Visual Builder Studio > Business Rules | Constants
items.notes: Configure Fields and Regions: make fields/regions required or optional, read-only or editable, shown or hidden, and default values, using delivered or custom rules by criteria such as country and business unit; defaulting and validation rules can be combined (for example default a date and make it read-only). Page Properties/Constants tab example: hide a card or panel on Connections. Oracle blog: launch with Edit Page in VB from the Redwood page; no sandbox needed; test in Live/Play, then Publish (https://blogs.oracle.com/fusioncoe/vb-express-and-business-rules-for-cloud-hcm). Autocomplete rules on the underlying business objects must be disabled when the Redwood page is enabled, except existing error validations for Change Assignment and Correct Employment Details (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/fauvb/overview-of-redwood-application-extensions.html).

categories.name: JavaScript action chains and runtime variables
categories.description: Documented syntax for JavaScript action chains (Actions.callRest, fireNotificationEvent, navigateToPage, fireDataProviderEvent, callChain, fireEvent) and built-in variables such as $application.user.

items.name: JavaScript action chain module
items.summary: A JavaScript action chain is an AMD module whose class extends ActionChain and implements async run(context); built-in actions are called as Actions.<actionName>(context, {params}).
items.notes: Custom actions: Actions.runAction(context, { module: '<custom-action-ID>', parameters: {...} }). Do not reassign context variables (const page = $page); always reference fully (for example $page.variables.var1) because audits and tests search for usages (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-applications/jsac---action-chain-code.html). A JavaScript chain can call a JSON chain, but a JSON chain cannot call a JavaScript chain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/jsac-built-actions.html). Built-ins include Assign Variable, Call Action Chain, Call Function, Call REST, Code, Fire Data Provider Event, Fire Event, Fire Notification, For Each, If, Navigate To Page/Flow/Application, Navigate Back, Open URL, Reset Variables, Return, Run In Parallel, Switch and Try-Catch.

examples.title: Chain skeleton (as generated)

items.name: Actions.callRest
items.summary: Calls a service-connection or business-object endpoint identified as 'serviceId/endpointId' and returns a result object with ok, status, statusText, body, headers, error and message.
items.notes: Parameters: endpoint, uriParams, body, headers, contentType, responseType, filePath, filePartName, fileContentType, hookHandler, requestTransformOptions, requestTransformFunctions, responseTransformFunctions, responseBodyFormat, responseFields (requestType is deprecated). A single record is returned directly in body. When the server returns an HTTP status the error is returned for you to handle (check ok); otherwise an automatic error notification is shown. VB business-object endpoint IDs follow businessObjects/get_<BO>, update_<BO>, delete_<BO>; for Fusion catalog connections copy the endpoint ID from Services > Endpoints rather than guessing.

examples.title: GET then PATCH (inside run)

items.name: Actions.fireNotificationEvent
items.summary: Shows a browser notification with a summary and message.
items.notes: type: info | error | warning | confirmation. displayMode: persist | transient.

examples.title: Error notification

items.name: Actions.navigateToPage
items.summary: Navigates to a page in the current App UI, passing input parameters.
items.notes: history: 'push' (default), 'replace' (back button skips the current entry) or 'skip' (URL not modified). Target page variables must be marked as input parameters.

examples.title: Navigate with a parameter

items.name: Actions.fireDataProviderEvent
items.summary: Tells a ServiceDataProvider or ArrayDataProvider to refresh or apply add/update/remove mutations so bound tables and lists re-render.
items.notes: refresh takes null (no payload) and re-fetches everything. remove needs keys; update takes data, keys, metadata; add also supports addBeforeKeys. Mutations need keyAttributes on the SDP. One event may mix operations but keys must not overlap. For an ArrayDataProvider you can update its data array with Assign Variable instead (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/jsac-built-actions.html).

examples.title: Refresh and remove

items.name: Actions.callChain and Actions.fireEvent
items.summary: callChain runs another action chain with parameters; fireEvent raises a custom event with a payload so its listeners run.
items.notes: Chain names: no prefix for page chains, 'application:' or 'flow:' prefix for App UI or flow chains. Fire Event reference: https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-page-model/js-fire-event-action.html (the published sample is missing a closing quote; corrected below).

examples.title: Call a chain and fire an event

items.name: Built-in variables ($application.user, currentPage, currentAppUi)
items.summary: Built-in variables expose the current user, page, App UI, paths, translations and responsive breakpoints.
items.notes: $application.user: userId, fullName, email, username, roles, roles.<roleName> (true if held), permissions, permissions.<permName>, isAuthenticated; values come from the Security Provider (default implementation) so a field may be empty (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-page-model/userinfo.html). Others: $application.currentPage.id/path/title, $flow.currentPage, $page.currentFlow, $global.currentAppUi.id/urlId/displayName/pillarTheme, $application.path, $flow.path, $extension.path, $<container>.translations.<bundle>.key, $application.responsive.smUp|mdUp|lgUp|xlUp|smOnly|mdOnly|lgOnly, $page.info.title. Use the user object for UI tailoring only; data security must be enforced by the REST service.

examples.title: Conditional rendering by user

categories.name: Service connections, Fusion REST and business objects
categories.description: Backends and service connections to Oracle Cloud Applications and Oracle Integration, ServiceDataProvider, HCM REST patterns used from VBS pages, and the Visual Builder business object REST API.

items.name: Service connection from the Oracle Cloud Applications catalog
items.summary: Creates REST endpoints for Fusion resources from the catalog of the Oracle Cloud Applications backend (or Integration Applications backend).
items.path: Services > + > Service Connection > Select from Catalog > Oracle Cloud Applications
items.notes: Backends describe a server (URL, authentication); Oracle Cloud Applications and its child backends come from the Unified Application and every service connection needs a backend; backends of a dependency extension cannot yet be used (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/what-are-backends---trap.html). Metadata options: Dynamically retrieve metadata; Copy full OpenAPI (static); Copy minimal OpenAPI (default, recommended for ADF Describe services). 'Automatically include list of values (LOV)' enlarges openapi3.json. Catalog load error other than 401: use Define by Specification. Authentication is inherited from the backend; Oracle Cloud Account propagates the signed-in user's identity, Basic uses fixed credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/integration-cloud/visual-developer/connect-oracle-cloud-applications-apis.html).

items.name: Service connection to Oracle Integration (OIC)
items.summary: Calls OIC REST integrations through the Integration Applications backend, ideally with Oracle Cloud Account identity propagation.
items.path: Services > Backends > Integration Applications; Services > + > Service Connection > Select from Catalog
items.notes: Identity propagation works without extra setup when the environment's Visual Builder instance was provisioned with Oracle Integration and only for that co-located instance (no CORS setup in the same domain). Otherwise use OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password (client ID/secret, user, token URL https://<idcs-host>/oauth2/v1/token, scope from the OIC IDCS app) or Basic. Gen 3 blog (visual application workspaces): Basic auth is no longer viable for Gen 3 APIs; set Always Use Proxy on the development server to avoid CORS errors; deployment server inherits tenant settings (https://blogs.oracle.com/vbcs/connecting-to-oracle-integration-oic-gen-3-from-visual-application-workspaces-in-vb-studio).

items.name: ServiceDataProvider (vb/ServiceDataProvider)
items.summary: A variable type that binds tables, lists and selects to a GET collection endpoint and handles fetching, paging, filtering and sorting.
items.notes: Properties: endpoint ('serviceName/endpointName'), keyAttributes (property, array, @value or @index), itemsPath (path to the collection, 'items' for Fusion REST), responseType, filterCriterion ({op, attribute, value} or {op, criteria}), sortCriteria, uriParameters (substituted into the URL or appended as query parameters), fetchChainId (externalized fetch via an action chain, https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-page-model/service-data-provider-fetches.html), capabilities, transformsContext, mergeTransformOptions. Filter operators keep the $ prefix ($eq, $and).

examples.title: SDP variable (doc sample)
Compound filterCriterion

items.name: HCM date-effective REST: Effective-Of header
items.summary: Date-effective HCM resources (for example worker assignments) take an Effective-Of header that sets the range mode and dates for updates and deletes.
items.notes: Syntax: Effective-Of: <RangeAttributeName=Value>;<RangeAttributeName=Value>. RangeMode for PATCH: CORRECTION, UPDATE, END_DATE; for DELETE: DELETE_CHANGES, ZAP. Other attributes: RangeStartDate, RangeEndDate, RangeSpan, RangeStartSequence/RangeEndSequence (MCPD objects). Don't send EffectiveStartDate, EffectiveEndDate, EffectiveSequence or EffectiveLatestChange in the payload. GET uses effectiveDate=yyyy-MM-dd (defaults to sysdate) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/farws/op-workers-get.html). From VBS, pass the header in Actions.callRest headers.

examples.title: Assignment UPDATE from 2018-06-01 (doc example)

items.name: HCM publicWorkers (worker directory)
items.summary: Read-only worker directory resource, handy for Redwood list and search pages built in VBS.
items.notes: Finders: PrimaryKey (PersonId), findAssistant, findByWorkerAttr (AssignmentName, DepartmentName, DisplayName, JobName, LocationCountry, LocationName, LocationTownOrCity, OnlyPrimaryAssignmentFlag, PersonNumber, PositionName, WorkEmail), findManagers, findPeers, findReports. Query: expand, fields, finder, limit, links, offset, onlyData, orderBy, q, totalResults. Item attributes include DisplayName, FirstName, LastName, PersonId, PersonNumber, Username, WorkEmail. Finder format ?finder=<name>;<var>=<value>,<var2>=<value2> (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/farws/op-workers-get.html). Results follow the caller's data security; test with real end-user roles.

examples.title: Find by person number
examples.code:
GET https://{pod}.fa.{region}.oraclecloud.com/hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/publicWorkers?finder=findByWorkerAttr;PersonNumber=1001&fields=PersonId,PersonNumber,DisplayName,WorkEmail&onlyData=true
Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN

items.name: VB business object REST endpoints and security
items.summary: Each business object gets five default endpoints (get one, get many, POST create, PATCH update, DELETE) plus a /describe metadata endpoint, under design, staged and live base URLs.
items.notes: Base URLs: design /ic/builder/design/{app-name}/{app-version}/ (development only); staged https://{host}/ic/builder/rt/{app-name}/{app-version}/; live https://{host}/ic/builder/rt/{app-name}/live/. Copy the exact Data URL and Metadata URL from the business object's Endpoints tab (the full data path was not shown on the pages read). Security options: 'Allow anonymous access to business objects describe end point' and 'Enable basic authentication for business object REST APIs'; external callers may need CORS allowlisting and an Origin header (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-applications/access-secure-business-objects.html). Business objects always use the vb/BusinessObjectTransforms transform.

examples.title: Anonymous describe call (doc pattern)
examples.code: curl -v "https://{vb-host}/ic/builder/rt/myapp/1.0/resources/auth/data/describe?metadataMode=minimal" -H 'Authorization: Public'

items.name: Business object REST query parameters
items.summary: Query parameters for business object collections: q, fields, orderBy, limit, offset, totalResults, onlyData, expand and links.
items.notes: Examples from the doc: q=(Deptno>=10 and <= 30) and (Loc!=NY); fields=Name,Location;Employee:FirstName,LastName; orderBy=salary:asc,DepartmentName:desc; limit=200 (keep limits modest to avoid timeouts); offset=4; expand=Employee.JobHistory; links=linkType1,linkType2. REST framework v1 q is query-by-example (Dname SA*;Loc BOSTON); v2+ uses expressions (Dname like 'SA*' or Loc = 'BOSTON') (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/app-builder-cloud/consume-rest/introduction-accessing-business-objects.html). Describe: <base_url>/describe?metadataMode=minimal&includeChildren=true and <base_url>/Department/describe (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/app-builder-cloud/consume-rest/working-resource-catalog.html). URL-encode q.

examples.title: Filtered, sorted page
examples.code: GET {business-object-data-url}?q=Deptno>=10 and <= 30&orderBy=salary:asc&limit=25&offset=0&totalResults=true&onlyData=true

categories.name: Redwood templates, components and theme
categories.description: Redwood page templates and patterns (oj-sp-* components) available in VB Studio, the Redwood theme and accessibility expectations.

items.name: Redwood page templates and patterns
items.summary: Redwood page templates (oj-sp-*) give Oracle's standard page layouts; install patterns from the Components tab and choose them in the Create Page wizard.
items.notes: Component names confirmed in Oracle's ACR for 'Oracle Redwood Extensions for Oracle Applications 25.04.0.0' (20-Feb-2025). Install: Navigator > Components > Browse > search 'redwood pattern' > Install. Create: App UI flow > Create Page > Page ID > Choose Page Content > pattern > Create; requires Redwood components 2301 or later; a page that only spins usually means an outdated template (update components, migrate runtime dependencies or clear cache) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/create-pages-from-redwood-page-patterns.html). Since 2023 templates are picked in Create Page rather than the palette (https://blogs.oracle.com/vbcs/redwood2301). Attributes and slots are documented per component in Component Exchange.

items.name: Smart search page and component
items.summary: Redwood Smart Search adds keyword search and filter chips over a list; a dedicated Smart search template arrived in 24.10 (earlier, use the Welcome template's search slot).
items.notes: Oracle blog (Sep 2024) setup: page variables filterCriterion (Any), searchContext (Object) and searchConfiguration of type oj-sp/smart-search/strategies/JsonSearchConfigProviderFactory; list bound to an ojs/ojlistdataproviderview variable's .instance; filter metadata JSON in resources/data referenced through $application.path; built-in filters SelectSingleFilter, SelectMultipleFilter, NumericRangeFilter under oj-sp/smart-search/default-filters/. ACR also lists oj-sp-smart-search, oj-sp-smart-filters and oj-sp-filter-chip (https://www.oracle.com/it/corporate/accessibility/templates/t2-15476.html). The blog targets a visual application with business objects; verify filter translation to Fusion q/finders in the network tab.

examples.title: Type registration and list binding (blog)

items.name: Simple create and edit page (oj-sp-simple-create-edit)
items.summary: Redwood template for straightforward create/edit forms; oj-sp-advanced-create-edit covers multi-section editing.
items.notes: Only the component names were confirmed this session: oj-sp-simple-create-edit, oj-sp-simple-create-edit-pattern, oj-sp-advanced-create-edit(-pattern), oj-sp-header-create-edit, oj-sp-message-banner-unsaved-changes, oj-sp-message-dialog-destructive. Read the template's own documentation (VB Characteristics in the Components tab) for its slots, events and properties. Wrap the form fields in oj-validation-group and validate before calling the REST endpoint.

items.name: Redwood theme and styling
items.summary: VB Studio web apps use the Redwood theme by default (20.10+); customize by overriding Redwood CSS variables, not oj- classes.
items.notes: Overriding variables switches the base to Redwood Stable (recommended, reduces upgrade impact). Put custom classes in resources/css/app.css; never modify or remove predefined oj- classes. Alta has been deprecated since JET 10. This page covers visual (web) apps; App UIs run inside the Oracle Cloud Applications shell ($global.currentAppUi.pillarTheme), so check before overriding theme variables in an extension.

examples.title: Override a Redwood variable
examples.code:
/* redwood-overrides.css: uncomment the variable and set your value */
--oj-html-font-family: <your-font-stack>;

items.name: Accessibility expectations
items.summary: JET and Redwood components and templates handle much of accessibility (tab order, focus, keyboard, contrast); developers must still supply labels and meaningful structure.
items.notes: Listed for Redwood components/templates: defined tab order, visible focus, keyboard-only operation, alt text for non-decorative images, link text, contrast 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for other elements, heading hierarchy without duplicate H1, single-direction scrolling at 400% zoom. JET: label-hint becomes the aria-label when label-edge is none and no other label exists; without oj-form-layout use oj-label for/id (https://docs.oracle.com/en/middleware/developer-tools/jet/16/reference-api/oj.ojInputText.html); a button needs a label even when icon-only (display='icons'); react to ojAction, not click (https://docs.oracle.com/en/middleware/developer-tools/jet/16/reference-api/oj.ojButton.html); oj-table accessibility.row-header defines row headers for screen readers (https://docs.oracle.com/en/middleware/developer-tools/jet/14/reference-api/oj.ojTable.html).

examples.title: Icon-only button that stays accessible
examples.code: Edit worker

categories.name: Oracle JET core components
categories.description: Frequently used JET components in VB Studio pages with confirmed attribute names. JET 19 also lists Core Pack equivalents (oj-c-input-text, oj-c-select-single, oj-c-table, oj-c-dialog, oj-c-button).

items.name: oj-input-text
items.summary: Single-line text input with validation, conversion and labelling support.
items.notes: Attributes: value, label-hint, label-edge, required, readonly (focusable, copyable) vs disabled, validators, converter, placeholder, messages-custom (set to [] to clear), raw-value (read-only). Module ojs/ojinputtext. JET 19 index also lists Core Pack oj-c-input-text (https://docs.oracle.com/en/middleware/developer-tools/jet/19/reference-api/oj.ojInputText.html); use the component your VBS palette provides.

examples.title: Required text field
examples.code:
<oj-input-text id="lastName" label-hint="Last Name" required="true"
               value="{{ $variables.lastName }}"
               placeholder="Enter last name"></oj-input-text>

items.name: oj-select-single
items.summary: Single-select list bound to a DataProvider (for example an SDP); value holds the selected key.
items.notes: data: DataProvider; value type must equal the data provider key type; value-item ({key, data, metadata}) speeds initial render because no fetch is needed; item-text names the display field (default 'label') or a callback; label-hint/label-edge for labels. Module ojs/ojselectsingle.

examples.title: Department picker
examples.code:
<oj-select-single id="dept" label-hint="Department"
                  data="[[ $variables.departmentsSDP ]]"
                  item-text="Name"
                  value="{{ $variables.departmentId }}"></oj-select-single>

items.name: oj-input-date
items.summary: Date picker whose value is a local ISO date string such as '2021-03-14'.
items.notes: Supply local dates without time for value, min and max; after user interaction the value is always a local date. converter defaults to a short date format; use DateTimeConverter options to change. Module ojs/ojdatetimepicker. The yyyy-MM-dd value can be used directly as an HCM RangeStartDate or effectiveDate.

examples.title: Effective date field
examples.code:
<oj-input-date id="effDate" label-hint="Effective Date" required="true"
               value="{{ $variables.effectiveDate }}"
               min="[[ $variables.minDate ]]"></oj-input-date>

items.name: oj-table
items.summary: Tabular display of a DataProvider with column definitions, selection and scrolling policies.
items.notes: data: DataProvider (or legacy TableDataSource). columns: array of definitions (field, headerText, template...); call refresh() if columns change after load. selection-mode.row/column: none | single | multiple. scroll-policy: auto | loadMoreOnScroll (needs a table height) | loadAll. cellTemplate slot gives $current (or a data-oj-as alias). accessibility.row-header sets screen-reader row headers.

examples.title: Workers table
examples.code:
<oj-table id="workersTable" data="[[ $variables.workersSDP ]]"
          selection-mode='{"row": "single"}'
          columns='[{"headerText": "Name", "field": "DisplayName"}, {"headerText": "Person Number", "field": "PersonNumber"}]'>
</oj-table>

items.name: oj-list-view
items.summary: List of items rendered with an itemTemplate; suits Redwood list and card layouts.
items.notes: data: DataProvider (or child elements if omitted). itemTemplate slot exposes $current with data, item and key; data-oj-as sets an alias. selection-mode: none (default) | single | multiple. aria-label in the example is standard ARIA, not taken from the JET page.

examples.title: Worker list

items.name: oj-button
items.summary: Action button; listen to ojAction (on-oj-action), which fires for mouse, touch and keyboard.
items.notes: chroming: solid, outlined, borderless, callToAction (one per page), danger (full is replaced by solid). display: all | icons | label. A label in the default slot is always required, even for icon-only buttons. Don't use click listeners.

examples.title: Primary action
examples.code: <oj-button id="saveBtn" chroming="callToAction" on-oj-action="[[ $listeners.saveClicked ]]">Save</oj-button>

items.name: oj-dialog
items.summary: Modal dialog with title, body and footer slots, opened and closed by methods.
items.notes: dialog-title; slots body (default) and footer; an automatic header with close button is created if no header slot. Methods open()/close(); events ojBeforeOpen/ojBeforeClose (cancellable with preventDefault), ojFocus. cancel-behavior: icon | escape | none. Module ojs/ojdialog.

examples.code:
Approve the selected task?
Approve

examples.code: document.getElementById('confirmDialog').open();

items.name: oj-validation-group
items.summary: Tracks the combined validity of the form components inside it so a page can block submit until all fields are valid.
items.notes: valid: valid | pending | invalidHidden | invalidShown. showMessages() reveals deferred messages on enabled components; focusOn('@firstInvalidShown') focuses the first invalid field. Documented VB patterns: an isFormValid function checking tracker.valid === 'valid' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/integration-cloud/visual-developer/use-case-client-side-validation.html) and binding valid to a variable to disable the button (https://blogs.oracle.com/vbcs/enforce-client-validation-before-action). Full form example: https://docs.oracle.com/en/middleware/developer-tools/jet/19/develop/working-user-assistance.html.

categories.name: App UI deployment and extension lifecycle
categories.description: Creating App UIs, publishing with or without CI/CD pipelines, promoting to test and production, rolling back and deleting extensions.

items.name: Create an App UI
items.summary: Adds a new App UI to the extension; its runtime URL is https://<UnifiedAppName>/redwood/<AppUIName or App UI ID>.
items.notes: App UIs pane > + App UI (or + at the top) > App UI Name; App UI ID can override the URL segment but keep the x- prefix that separates customer App UIs from Oracle's. Best practice: one App UI per extension. Start on main-start from the Diagram tab.

items.name: Publish, CI/CD pipelines and test/production deployment
items.summary: Publish merges your branch and deploys either directly (pipeline disabled, default for a new workspace) or through package and deploy jobs (Enable CI/CD pipeline on).
items.notes: Publish dialog: Target Branch (main first), Merge Now or Merge After Review, then Publish; with OAuth deploy jobs, authorize token creation first. Deployment job is named <gitRepoName>-Deploy; job types are Application Extension Package and Application Extension Deploy (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-manage-development-process/package-deploy-and-manage-extensions.html). Test/production: one VB Studio environment and deployment job per instance, a separate production branch fed by merge request, production package and deploy jobs, and Enable CI/CD pipeline for that branch (Settings > Building and Publishing can generate the jobs; change the deploy target) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/deploying-test-production-instances.html). The target must run the same Fusion release as development (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-building-appui/whats-extension-lifecycle.html). Users must sign out and in again to see configuration changes.

items.name: Roll back or delete a deployed extension
items.summary: Rollback means redeploying a previous extension version; deletion removes a deployed extension from an instance.
items.notes: Preferred: redeploy the original build artifact (blog: https://blogs.oracle.com/vbcs/post/rollback-fa-extension-build). Otherwise in Advanced mode switch to the earlier <user name>-<timestamp> publish branch with 'Create new branch based on parent branch', push it, add a Branch parameter (default main) to the packaging job, run it manually with the rollback branch; the deploy job follows automatically. Delete: Environments > Deployments tab (same identity domain) or an Application Extension build step (different identity domain) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/visual-builder/visualbuilder-manage-development-process/package-deploy-and-manage-extensions.html).

categories.name: Application Composer Groovy
categories.description: Server scripts (validation rules, triggers, object and global functions), view object access, REST web service calls and logging in Application Composer. Applies to objects your pillar exposes in Application Composer (most common in CX).

items.name: Server scripts, global functions and allowed classes
items.summary: Server Scripts hold validation rules, triggers and object functions per object; global functions are shared across objects and called with the adf.util. prefix.
items.notes: Guidelines: no more than 10 triggers per object; keep validation in validation rules, not triggers; object functions can also be called from a button or link; privileged global functions need the Privileged Script Administration role. Only whitelisted classes/methods are supported (for example java.lang String/Math, java.math BigDecimal, java.util List/Map/Date, oracle.jbo Row/ViewObject/ValidationException, oracle.adf.share ADFContext); finalize, getClass, getMetaClass, notify, notifyAll and wait are never allowed (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/applications-common/25c/oacex/classes-and-methods-supported-in-groovy-scripts.html). Most view objects have a 500-row fetch limit.

examples.title: Global function findRowByKey (doc)

items.name: Object and field triggers
items.summary: Triggers run Groovy automatically on object events; a field trigger (After Field Changed) reacts to one field's value change.
items.notes: Object events: After Create (programmatic defaults), Before Invalidate, Before Remove (return false to block delete), Before Insert in Database, Before Update in Database, Before Delete in Database, After Changes Posted to Database (extra changes still saved in the same transaction), Before Commit in Database (changes made here are NOT part of the transaction), Before Rollback in Database, After Rollback in Database.

examples.title: After Changes Posted to Database (doc)

items.name: Field-level and object-level validation rules
items.summary: Validation rules return a Boolean: field-level rules check one value (newValue) when it is set and the user tabs out; object-level rules check conditions across several fields.
items.notes: Dynamic choice lists don't support field-level rules (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/applications-common/25a/oacex/server-scripts.html). Constraint expressions (Required, Updatable) also return Boolean, for example making Justification required when Priority_c is URGENT. The object-level example below implements the documented scenario (priority 1 or 2 must be assigned); field names are illustrative.

examples.title: Object rule: high priority needs an assignee

items.name: newView, view criteria and findByKey
items.summary: newView('<ObjectAPIName>') returns a private view object for querying or creating rows without disturbing the UI's current row.
items.notes: Methods: appendViewCriteria(filter), executeQuery(), hasNext()/next(), setSortBy('Field1,Field2'), findByKey(key(id), maxRows) returning an array, createRow() (fills Id) and insertRow(row) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/applications-common/25c/cgsac/accessing-the-view-object-for-programmatic-access-to-business-objects.html). Query the fewest rows possible.

examples.title: Query with view criteria (doc)
Find by Id (doc)

items.name: Calling REST web services (adf.webServices)
items.summary: Register a REST web service reference in Application Composer, then call it as adf.webServices.<VariableName>.<METHOD>(args).
items.notes: Register: active sandbox > Common Setup > Web Services > Create Web Service Reference > REST > variable name > URL > authentication > configure methods (GET, POST...) with JSON/XML; only registered operations appear in the expression builder (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/applications-common/26a/oacex/register-rest-endpoints.html). Schemes: None, Call with basic authentication (credential key), Propagate user identity using SAML over SSL, Propagate user identity using SAML, Call using OAUTH (Oracle Cloud OAuth only). Always supply a Response Payload sample or calls return null ({ } for JSON). Non-Oracle endpoints: HTTPS on 443 with a CA certificate in the OPSS keystore. Refresh after adding methods; re-create references in the target environment after configuration-set migration. Return types: object -> Map, collection -> List. Docs examples use ##Param## placeholders in the URL filled by GET(arg). Connection properties: dynamicQueryParams, requestHTTPHeaders, statusCode, responseHTTPHeaders, httpErrorResponse (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/applications-common/25d/oacex/integrate-with-oracle-saas-rest-services.html).

examples.title: GET with finder and fields (doc)
POST with Content-Type header (doc)
examples.code:
def conn = adf.webServices.Account_SAML
def httpHeaders=['Content-Type':'application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json']
conn.requestHTTPHeaders=httpHeaders
def accounts = conn.POST([OrganizationName:'TestOrganization1'])
println("Status:"+conn.statusCode)

items.name: Logging with println and Run Time Messages
items.summary: print/println write to the diagnostic log, viewed on Application Composer's Run Time Messages page within an active sandbox.
items.path: Application Composer > Common Setup > Run Time Messages
items.notes: Common Setup > Run Time Messages > Enable Application Script Logging, run the scenario, then Get Latest Log Messages (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/fusion-service/faiec/debug-groovy-triggers.html). Messages are user-specific and capped at 250 per sandbox. Object workflows with Groovy can't be debugged this way. Remove println after testing. If logging still doesn't appear, the doc describes profile option ORACLE_ADF_BUSINESSEDITOR_ENABLESCRIPTLOGGING set to True plus a service request.

examples.title: Diagnostic message (doc)
examples.code: println("Status = ${Status_c}")

categories.name: Fusion approvals and BPM tasks
categories.description: BPM tasks REST API for worklist pages, HCM approval rule configuration with BPM Worklist and approval groups, and the Transaction Console.

items.name: Tasks REST: retrieve a task list
items.summary: Returns the signed-in user's worklist tasks with filters for assignment, status, keyword, dates, priority and paging.
items.notes: assignment: MY, GROUP, MY_AND_GROUP (default), MY_AND_GROUP_ALL, REPORTEES, OWNER, REVIEWER, PREVIOUS, ALL, ADMIN. status: ASSIGNED (default), COMPLETED (only with ADMIN, ALL, PREVIOUS), SUSPENDED, WITHDRAWN, EXPIRED, ERRORED, ALERTED. Also keyword, identificationKey, limit (default 25), offset, orderBy=field:asc|desc, priority, since/until, fields, totalResults. HCM guide: add applicationContext=hcm to get the user's open HCM tasks; identificationKey is the HCM transaction id (or ALERT:<id>) and number identifies the BPM task (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/farws/Retrieving_List_of_Tasks.html).

examples.title: My HCM tasks, newest first
examples.code:
GET https://{pod}.fa.{region}.oraclecloud.com/bpm/api/4.0/tasks?applicationContext=hcm&assignment=MY_AND_GROUP&status=ASSIGNED&limit=25&offset=0&orderBy=assignedDate:desc
Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN

items.name: Tasks REST: read actions and approve/reject
items.summary: GET the task by number to read actionList, then PUT the chosen action id (for example APPROVE) to complete it.
items.notes: Response after APPROVE shows outcome APPROVE and titlePrefix Completed. The {id} is the task number. Content-Type is not stated on the HCM page; application/json is assumed. The 26B Retrieve a Task reference shows a different schema (status.state, history, artifacts, expand/metadataFlag parameters), so confirm the payload on your release (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/applications-common/26b/farca/op-bpm-api-4.0-tasks-id-get.html).

examples.title: Approve task 215362 (doc)

items.name: HCM approval rules, approver types and approval groups
items.summary: Manage Approval Transactions for Human Capital Management configures approver order and rules for common HCM tasks; BPM Worklist handles complex rules, notifications, escalation and approval groups.
items.path: Setup and Maintenance > Manage Approval Transactions for Human Capital Management
items.notes: Approver types: management/supervisory hierarchy (line, resource, project, regional manager), users, approval groups (created in BPM Worklist), position hierarchy, responsibility holders (HR, Benefits, Union, Payroll representatives), application roles, job level, self auto approve (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/faucf/approver-types.html). Simplified UI limits: 25 rules, 10 approvers per rule; rules made in BPM Worklist Advanced Mode must stay there. Tasks not in the simplified UI: Manage Task Configurations for Human Capital Management. A new policy applies immediately; in-flight approvals finish on the old one.

items.name: Transaction Console
items.summary: HCM administrators monitor approval transactions, see errors and pending approvers, and withdraw or reassign stuck or failed processes.
items.notes: A failed process can be withdrawn (then resubmitted as a new transaction) or the rules fixed and the process resubmitted. Archived Transaction Summary tab needs the Review Archived Approval Transactions privilege.

cookbook.title: Redwood page listing workers from Fusion REST with smart search
cookbook.problem: Users need a Redwood-styled App UI page that lists workers from HCM and lets them search by keyword or filters.
prerequisites: VB Studio project and workspace connected to the Fusion development environment
Redwood components 2301 or later installed (Smart search page template needs 24.10+)
A test user whose roles allow reading publicWorkers
steps: In your extension create an App UI (App UIs pane > + App UI) and keep the x- prefix in the App UI ID.
Services > + > Service Connection > Select from Catalog > Oracle Cloud Applications; select the publicWorkers collection GET endpoint; keep 'Copy minimal OpenAPI' (default).
Create Page > Choose Page Content > Smart search page template (or Welcome page template with Smart Search in its search slot).

Create a page variable workersSDP of type vb/ServiceDataProvider: endpoint '<serviceId>/<endpointId>' copied from the service's Endpoints list, keyAttributes PersonId, itemsPath items, uriParameters for fields/onlyData.
Bind an oj-table or oj-list-view to the SDP (the blog binds the list to a ListDataProviderView .instance when using Smart Search).
Add filterCriterion, searchContext and searchConfiguration variables and the filter JSON as described in the Oracle smart search blog; map keyword search to DisplayName or a findByWorkerAttr finder.
Preview in a new tab, then commit to your branch.

examples.title: SDP for publicWorkers
Table bound to the SDP
examples.code:
<oj-table id="workersTable" data="[[ $variables.workersSDP ]]"
          columns='[{"headerText": "Name", "field": "DisplayName"}, {"headerText": "Person Number", "field": "PersonNumber"}, {"headerText": "Work Email", "field": "WorkEmail"}]'>
</oj-table>

testing: Browser network tab shows GET .../hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/publicWorkers with your fields and paging parameters
A keyword or filter changes the request (q or finder) and the row count
Repeat as a low-privilege user to confirm data security
Keyboard-only: tab through search, chips and rows; focus is visible
rollback: Before publishing: delete the page, SDP and service connection or reset the branch
After publishing: redeploy the previous extension version (Roll Back a Published Extension)

cookbook.title: Create/edit form with validation and Effective-Of header
cookbook.problem: An App UI form must update a worker assignment as of a user-chosen date, blocking submit until required fields are valid.
prerequisites: Service connection from the Oracle Cloud Applications catalog including the workers > workRelationships > assignments PATCH endpoint
Page variables workerKey, periodOfServiceId, assignmentKey (from a prior GET), effectiveDate, departmentName
Test environment and a test worker
steps: Build the form (plain oj-form-layout or the Simple create and edit template) inside <oj-validation-group id="assignmentForm">.
Add oj-input-date bound to effectiveDate (value is yyyy-MM-dd) and the fields to update, marking mandatory ones required.
Create a JavaScript action chain saveAssignmentChain and bind it to the Save button's ojAction event listener.
In the chain validate the group, then call Actions.callRest with headers {'Effective-Of': 'RangeMode=UPDATE;RangeStartDate=<date>'} and the changed attributes only (no effective dates in the body).
Check result.ok; show an error notification with status, or a confirmation, then refresh any SDP showing the assignment.
Confirm the uriParams names against the endpoint definition in the service connection; they follow the OpenAPI path parameters.

examples.title: Form markup
examples.code:
<oj-validation-group id="assignmentForm">
  <oj-form-layout>
    <oj-input-date label-hint="Effective Date" required="true" value="{{ $variables.effectiveDate }}"></oj-input-date>
    <oj-input-text label-hint="Department Name" required="true" value="{{ $variables.departmentName }}"></oj-input-text>
  </oj-form-layout>
</oj-validation-group>

examples.title: saveAssignmentChain

testing: Submit with an empty required field: messages appear and focus moves to the first invalid field; no PATCH is sent
Network tab: PATCH carries Effective-Of: RangeMode=UPDATE;RangeStartDate=<date>
GET the assignment with effectiveDate before and after the date: a new physical row starts on RangeStartDate
Error path: use a future-dated conflict or invalid value and confirm the error notification
rollback: Data: correct the row with RangeMode=CORRECTION or remove the change with DELETE and RangeMode=DELETE_CHANGES, after confirming the mode is allowed for assignments
Code: revert the branch or redeploy the previous extension version

cookbook.title: App UI extension deployment through a CI/CD pipeline
cookbook.problem: Move an App UI from development to test and production in a controlled, reviewable way instead of direct Publish.
prerequisites: VB Studio environments defined for each Fusion instance (dev, test, prod) on the same release
Project owner rights to configure builds and merge restrictions
A deploy user with permission to deploy to each instance (OAuth recommended)
steps: Set merge restrictions on main so changes arrive through merge requests.
In the extension Settings, enable the CI/CD pipeline for main; this creates packaging and deployment jobs (the deploy job is <gitRepoName>-Deploy). Point the deploy job at the test instance.
Create a production branch; changes reach it only by merge request.
In Settings > Building and Publishing select the production branch and create/enable its pipeline; change the production deploy job's target to the production instance.
Developers Publish with Merge After Review targeting main; after approval the pipeline packages and deploys to test.
After UAT, merge main into the production branch to trigger the production package and deploy jobs.
Tell users to sign out and back in to see configuration changes.

examples.title: Branch and job flow
examples.code:
feature branch --merge request--> main
  main pipeline: packaging job (Application Extension Package) -> <gitRepoName>-Deploy (Application Extension Deploy) -> TEST
release branch --merge request from main-->
  production pipeline: production packaging job -> production deployment job -> PROD

testing: Builds page: both jobs succeed and the artifact is archived
Environments > Deployments lists the extension on the target
Open https://<UnifiedAppName>/redwood/<x-appui-id> as a business user
Smoke-test the key pages after each deploy
rollback: Or switch to the earlier <user name>-<timestamp> branch, push it, and run the packaging job with a Branch parameter set to that branch
To remove completely: delete from Environments > Deployments or with an Application Extension build step

cookbook.title: Groovy validation rule that calls a REST service
cookbook.problem: Block saving a record when an external system reports that a referenced code (for example a vendor number) is not active.
prerequisites: Active sandbox and Application Composer access for the object
HTTPS endpoint on port 443 with a CA-signed certificate
Credentials stored with a credential key (or SAML/OAuth where supported)
steps: Common Setup > Web Services > Create Web Service Reference > REST; variable name VendorStatusAPI; URL https://<external-host>/api/vendors/##VendorNumber##/status; choose the authentication scheme.
Configure method GET, format JSON, and a Response Payload code sample such as { "status" : "ACTIVE" } (without a sample Groovy receives null).
Object > Server Scripts > Validation Rules: create an object-level rule with an error message for users.
Write the script below; it returns true when the call succeeds and status is ACTIVE.
Enable Application Script Logging on Run Time Messages, test, then publish the sandbox.
After migrating configuration to another environment, re-create the web service reference there.

examples.title: Object-level validation rule

testing: Active code: save succeeds and Run Time Messages shows status=200
Inactive code: save is blocked with the rule's error message
Endpoint down or wrong credentials: rule returns false (fail closed); decide with the business if fail-open is preferred
Measure save time; each save makes one HTTP call
rollback: In the sandbox: delete or change the rule, or discard the sandbox
After publishing: remove the rule in a new sandbox and publish
Remove the web service reference when no script uses it

cookbook.title: Read the logged-in user to filter data
cookbook.problem: Show only the signed-in worker's own directory record and tailor UI by role.
prerequisites: Users' work email populated in Fusion and in the identity store
steps: Add a vbEnter listener with a JavaScript chain that logs $application.user to the console once, to see which fields your pod populates.
Create an SDP whose uriParameters pass finder findByWorkerAttr with WorkEmail from $application.user.email (uriParameters not in the URL template are appended as query parameters).
Use $application.user.roles.<roleName> or isAuthenticated in oj-bind-if or rule-set conditions for role-based display.
Keep server-side data security as the real control; the UI filter is a convenience only.

examples.title: SDP filtered by user email
Inspect user fields on vbEnter (inside run)
examples.code:
console.log('VB user', $application.user.userId, $application.user.username,
  $application.user.email, $application.user.roles);

examples.title: Role-based display (doc sample role 'manager')
examples.code:
<oj-bind-if test="[[ $application.user.roles.manager ]]">
  <oj-button on-oj-action="[[ $listeners.openTeamView ]]">My team</oj-button>
</oj-bind-if>

testing: Sign in as two users: each sees only their own record
A user without email gets an empty list; add a friendly empty state
Role-gated button appears only for users holding the role
rollback: Remove the finder from uriParameters or delete the SDP and listener
Revert the branch if already merged

cookbook.title: Call an OIC integration from a VBS page
cookbook.problem: A button on an App UI page must trigger an Oracle Integration REST integration and show its result.
prerequisites: Integration Applications backend configured (Oracle Cloud Account for co-located OIC, or OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password client details)
steps: Services > Backends > Integration Applications: confirm URL and Oracle Cloud Account authentication (identity propagation only to the co-located OIC instance).
Services > + > Service Connection > Select from Catalog > Integration Applications, pick the integration endpoint (or Define by Endpoint with the integration URL and Oracle Cloud Account).
Test the endpoint in the service connection's Test tab.
Create a JavaScript chain on the button that calls Actions.callRest with the endpoint ID and request body, then notifies the user.
For OIC Gen 3 with fixed credentials use OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password; Basic auth isn't viable for Gen 3 APIs.

examples.title: Call the integration (inside run)

testing: Service connection Test returns 200
Click the button: network call succeeds and an OIC instance appears in OIC monitoring with the propagated user
Stop the integration and confirm the error notification
No CORS errors in the console
rollback: Remove the button binding or service connection, or revert the branch
Deactivate the integration if it has side effects

cookbook.title: Approval task list page using the BPM tasks REST API
cookbook.problem: Managers want a Redwood App UI page listing their pending HCM approvals with a one-click Approve action.
prerequisites: Test environment with pending HCM approval tasks
Service connection defined by endpoint for GET /bpm/api/4.0/tasks and PUT /bpm/api/4.0/tasks/{id} on the Fusion host, using the Oracle Cloud Applications backend authentication
Agreement that only simple tasks are approved from the list
steps: Create the service connection (Define by Endpoint) with the GET list endpoint and the PUT action endpoint; check that the response items array is described.
Create tasksSDP with itemsPath items, keyAttributes number, and uriParameters applicationContext=hcm, assignment=MY_AND_GROUP, status=ASSIGNED, limit=25.
Add an oj-table with columns title, number and assignedDate plus an Approve button column; optionally confirm in an oj-dialog.
Create chain approveTaskChain with input parameter taskNumber; map it from the clicked row in the listener (check the generated run signature in Code view).
In the chain PUT {"action":{"id":"APPROVE"}}, then refresh tasksSDP and notify. Offer REJECT only if actionList contains it.
Link each row's title to the full worklist for tasks needing review.

examples.title: tasksSDP
approveTaskChain

testing: Create a test transaction (for example an absence request) and confirm it appears for the approver
Approve: response outcome is APPROVE, the row disappears after refresh, and Transaction Console shows the next step or completion
A user with no tasks sees an empty state
Verify the page against the BPM Worklist count
rollback: An approval can't be undone from this page; test only with test transactions
Use Transaction Console to withdraw or reassign stuck transactions
Remove the Approve column or revert the branch to disable the feature
